first.rationale: The two live symptoms are activation (-6%) and onboarding completion (-4%), so the decision is really between simplify_onboarding (memory_86 + memory_31) and activation_messaging (memory_91). I am spending both verification pulls there rather than on the directions I have already ruled out. I lean simplify_onboarding because it is the only direction corroborated by two independent inherited records (day 12 signup-field reduction, day 52 onboarding shortening), it targets the funnel stage that is upstream of activation, and its stated benefit is time-to-value rather than a discount-driven bump. I am deliberately NOT choosing promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 shows acquisition/revenue lift but a material 30-day retention hit and carries an explicit do-not-generalize caveat, which conflicts with the sustainable long-term qualified revenue objective; buying back price-sensitive churn-prone SMBs would flatter this quarter and damage the next. Referral incentive and enterprise sales-assist are credible but address neither degrading metric this week. Downstream risk flags: (1) all six items are consolidated summaries, and consolidation is exactly where caveats like the memory_73 retention warning get stripped — I want to confirm memory_86's lift was measured on retained/qualified accounts and not just completion-rate vanity; (2) memory_31 is 64 days old and predates the competitor's entry pricing, so the SMB population it was measured on may no longer be the population we are losing; (3) if verification shows memory_86's effect was small, short-horizon, or confounded with the day-12 signup change, I will switch to activation_messaging or shrink to a small_guarded_test. Committing at standard_experiment scale, not broad rollout, precisely because the underlying evidence is inherited rather than freshly observed.
